title: Fleet Gauge: Operator Safeguard & Scaling Tooling in Console
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a new Console surface called 'Fleet Gauge' that unifies fleet-level scaling controls, throughput guarantees, and change history into a single operator-facing workflow. The goal is to give platform operators and fleet owners a concise way to: 1) view current throughput vs SLA commitments (p50/p95 latency and tokens/s), 2) edit and preview autoscaling policies (min/max, cooldown windows, prioritized routes), and 3) review a changelog of provisioning and policy edits with rollback affordances. This ticket covers product spec, UX flows for live editing and simulation, acceptance criteria, and coordination items for engineering and design. Emphasis on clear failure modes (what happens on evictions, quota exhaustion) and auditability (immutable change events, links to incident runbooks).
acceptance_criteria: Fleet Gauge dashboard card visible for Dedicated deployments with >1 capacity pool
Throughput view shows live tokens/s, 5m/1h trends, and SLA overlay (configurable), with p50/p95 latency bands
Autoscale editor supports policy presets, custom rules (CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/s target), and a simulation mode showing projected capacity & cost delta
Change history shows user, timestamp, diff, and provides a one-click rollback that creates a reversible 'revert' change event
RBAC: only users with 'fleet-operator' role can save policy changes; all changes emit audit entries to configured audit sink
Telemetry: events emitted for edits, simulations, rollbacks, and policy-triggered autoscale actions (telemetry names + schema defined)
updates: 2025-02-12 - Maya Chen created initial PRD after discovery with two enterprise customers requiring SLA visibility and reversible scaling actions.

2025-02-28 - Prototype validated in staging against a synthetic workload; autoscale simulation produced sensible capacity projections but surfaced a confusing 'cost delta' metric — Design to refine wording.
2025-03-01 - Security review kickoff: security requested KMS-backed signing for rollback actions; scope added to ENG-58012.
2025-03-03 - PM review: finalized acceptance criteria and added telemetry naming conventions. Draft GitHub PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/7483
notes: Key UX constraint: surface only high-value knobs (target tokens/s and safety buffers) for majority users; expose advanced rule DSL behind 'advanced' toggle. Provide simulation with cost estimate and confidence band. Plan to instrument canary fleets for 2 weeks before org-wide rollout.
